newsitem.title: USA: MCI says going "straight ahead" with BT merger.
newsitem.headline: MCI says going "straight ahead" with BT merger.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp is "going straight ahead" with its merger plans with British Telecommunications Plc despite steep losses the U.S. carrier is running up in the local phone market, the company's president said Tuesday.
MCI President Timothy Price also repeated that the No. 2 long-distance carrier's losses in the local market could hit $800 million this year and exceed that amount in 1998.
"We may lose more than that in the local busines next year," Price said in a speech to the Economic Strategy Institute, an economic think tank based in Washington.
Price declined to say whether MCI's proposed merger with BT may be restructured because of the losses.

"We are going straight ahead with the merger," he said. Price also said he expects to be running MCI for a "long" time, rebutting suggestions that he may be forced to step down because of the carrier's red ink in the local business.

Price also stepped up calls for federal and state phone regulators and antitrust regulators to take more active steps to open the local phone monopolies controlled by the regional Baby Bell phone companies.
"We will provide competition to the local monopolies. All we ask is that the regulators do their job," he said, urging regulators to penalize local carriers that obstruct competition.

Price applauded comments by FCC Chairman Reed Hundt, who called for creation of a task force to investigate charges that the Bells are thwarting competition. Hundt made his comments in an interview in Tuesday's edition of USA Today.
